headline: Mistakes Businesses Make When Trying to Get AI Citations
articleBody: It's easy to make some missteps when you're trying to get AI systems to cite your business. A pretty common mistake we see is using vague, marketing-speak headings like 'Solutions' or 'Our Services.' While humans might get it, AI systems are looking for headings that mirror actual questions people ask, like 'What are the benefits of [your service]?' or 'How much does [your product] cost?'. If your headings aren't clear questions, AI has a harder time matching them to user prompts. Another big one is burying the lead! AI wants direct answers, usually in the first sentence or two of a section, not after three paragraphs of introduction. If the main answer to a question is hidden deep within a long paragraph, AI might just skip it. Many businesses also overlook the power of FAQ sections and schema markup. AI engines heavily rely on explicit question-and-answer pairs, so not having clear FAQs or applying FAQ schema is a real missed opportunity. It's like having a treasure map but forgetting to mark the 'X.' Ignoring technical foundations, such as proper schema markup, ensuring your 'dateModified' is updated, or making sure search engine crawlers can access your pages, also hurts. These elements might seem minor, but they significantly impact how easily AI can process your content. Lastly, businesses often forget to strengthen their trust signals. Things like citing external authoritative sources, providing statistics, or including author credentials can make AI much more confident in recommending your business. Avoiding these common mistakes can really boost your chances of getting cited by AI.
